{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|Sandwiches]]

A '''Monte Cristo sandwich''' is a [[Cookbook:Sandwiches|sandwich]] composed of ham, chicken, and Swiss cheese enclosed in bread that is dipped in beaten egg and fried until golden brown. <ref>Encyclopedia of American Food and Drink, John F. Mariani [Lebhar-Friedman:New York] 1999 (p. 209)</ref>

==Ingredients==
* [[Cookbook:Butter|Butter]]
* 3 slices of white [[Cookbook:bread|bread]]
* [[Cookbook:Slicing|Sliced]] lean baked [[Cookbook:ham|ham]]
* Sliced cooked [[Cookbook:chicken|chicken]]
* Thinly-sliced [[Cookbook:Emmental Cheese|Emmental cheese]]
* [[Cookbook:egg|Egg]] [[Cookbook:batter|batter]]

==Procedure==

# Butter the first slice of bread and cover with ham and chicken.
# Butter the middle slice on both sides, place on meat, and cover with cheese.
# Butter the third slice and place, butter down, over cheese.
# Trim crusts, then cut sandwich in two and secure with [[Cookbook:Skewer|toothpicks]]
# Dip in light egg batter, and [[Cookbook:Frying|fry]] in butter on all sides until golden brown.
# Remove toothpicks and serve with currant jelly, strawberry jam, or cranberry sauce.<ref>The Brown Derby Cookbook [Doubleday & Company:Garden City NY] 1949 (p. 183)</ref>
